title: Thor Henning Hetland
description: Software architect, AI development pioneer, founder of JavaZone and eXOReaction

items.title: Cloud Computing: Are You Looking for IaaS or PaaS Provider?
items.content_html: Comparing IaaS and PaaS cloud models from Amazon, Google, and Microsoft -- and why the choice between platform and infrastructure shapes everything.

items.title: Clouded Vision
items.content_html: Cloud savings come from zero-admin architecture, not cheaper servers. Most apps carry enterprise DNA that makes migration painful without rethinking the design.

items.title: Open Source and Community Clouds
items.content_html: Early open-source cloud platforms StratusLab and Eucalyptus offered EC2-compatible infrastructure on your own hardware, with real management challenges.

items.title: Sinnataggen and some Cloud development thoughts...
items.content_html: Gartner's six criteria for evaluating cloud development platforms, from interoperability and mobile support to vendor longevity and ecosystem quality.

items.title: Trouble In The Clouds - Gmail Turns Into Gfail
items.content_html: Gmail's February 2009 outage exposed cloud reliability gaps and Google's slow communication -- three hours before acknowledging a widespread service failure.

items.title: Why clouds should be more like operating systems
items.content_html: Managing multiple AMIs still requires manual sysadmin. Clouds need dashboard tooling and automated administration to deliver on their promise.

items.title: Its time for auto scaling - avoid peak load provisioning for web applications
items.content_html: Applications cannot use new compute resources dynamically without middleware virtualisation. Auto-scaling requires architecture, not just infrastructure.

items.title: Cloud - auto-magic or just provisioning platform for your distributed system
items.content_html: Clouds are provisioning platforms, not silver bullets. Enterprises still want magic, but the real question is whether to educate or go with the flow.

items.title: Gartner on Cloud Computing, misses again...
items.content_html: Gartner's five cloud attributes conflate delivery models, deployment models, and key characteristics into a flat taxonomy that obscures more than it reveals.

items.title: On the greenness of Clouds
items.content_html: Cloud computing is greener than in-house servers today, but componentisation drives consumption. If computation gets too cheap to measure, waste will follow.

items.title: Production Scars Are Architecture
items.content_html: Six architectural lessons from running an autonomous AI agent in production. Each scar is a failure category surprising enough to force mechanical change. Prose governance didn't work — here's what did.

items.title: Your AI Agent Does Not Know the Law (and How to Fix That)
items.content_html: Your AI agent will confidently tell a customer they're GDPR-compliant when they're not. Here's the architecture that fixes that.

items.title: The Zombie in the Basement
items.content_html: Static architecture catalogs document what someone knew at a point in time. Betonix GmbH thought they had 23 database connections. They had 52. The migration nearly shipped that delta.

items.title: Frøya: A Digital Co-Worker
items.content_html: Quadim's AI agent Froya maintains a public skill library at scale -- not replacing a human editor, but making continuous QA possible where none existed before.

items.title: Mapping Human Potential
items.content_html: Static skill taxonomies fail because skills are contextual. Quadim uses RAG, MCP, and dynamic taxonomies to build maps that adapt to their users.

items.title: Rethinking Systems for AI
items.content_html: AI asks why, not what. Systems designed for current-state queries need three shifts -- events over state, graphs over tables, conversations over queries.

items.title: Aurora: Answering Why
items.content_html: Aurora combines a temporal graph database with an AI query layer to answer why questions -- pattern detection, forensic investigation, and ripple effects.

items.title: Unlocking Temporal Graphs
items.content_html: A bitemporal model with four time dimensions -- transaction, valid, decision, and query -- enables perfect past recall and repeatable historical reporting.

items.title: From Data to Action: The Alchemy and Aurora Stack
items.content_html: Alchemy handles reactive data ingestion via YAML config; Aurora stores temporal graph events. Two layers, independently scalable, cleanly separated.

items.title: The Organisational Amnesia Problem
items.content_html: Most systems overwrite history, making root cause analysis painfully manual. Temporal graphs make those questions answerable in seconds across six domains.
